# Ghost-AOS Git-Bus Treaty — LAW Record Integration (`mag/law.py`)

## Mechanism in four lines

Workers never talk to each other. They talk only to the **git bus**: proposals, votes, and seals are refs. Every worker is stateless — it derives everything from refs, re-executes everything locally against a pinned toolchain, and signs what it observes. One voice exists because quorum intersection makes two certified truths impossible, and no drift exists because any worker whose output deviates from deterministic re-execution collects fewer than Q votes and its branch dies childless. The voice is the sealed ref chain: `refs/bus/seal/N`.

---

## 1. Registry plumbing (drop into `mag/law.py`)

```python
# ── mag/law.py · enforcement registry ────────────────────────────────────────
from __future__ import annotations
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import IntEnum
import hashlib, json, re, sys

class Tier(IntEnum):
    KERNEL = 0      # non-bypassable; violation freezes the entire bus
    HARD   = 1      # violation rejects the offending operation
    SOFT   = 2      # violation logs + warns

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LawRecord:
    id:        str
    trigger:   tuple[str, ...]
    condition: tuple[str, ...]   # named predicates; ALL must hold
    action:    dict[str, str]    # outcome -> enforcement behavior
    guardrail: tuple[str, ...]   # invariants that hold even while acting
    tier:      Tier

_REGISTRY: dict[str, LawRecord] = {}

def register(law: LawRecord) -> None:
    if law.id in _REGISTRY:
        raise ValueError(f"duplicate law id: {law.id}")
    _REGISTRY[law.id] = law

# ── constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q = lambda n: -(((2 * n) + 1) // -3)      # ceil((2N+1)/3); tolerates f=⌊(N-1)/3⌋
EPOCH_DEADLINE_TICKS = 512                 # journal ticks — NEVER wall clock

REF_GRAMMAR = {
    "proposal": r"^refs/bus/proposals/(?P<epoch>\d+)/(?P<wid>w\d{2})$",
    "vote":     r"^refs/bus/votes/(?P<epoch>\d+)/(?P<root>[0-9a-f]{64})/(?P<wid>w\d{2})\.sig$",
    "seal":     r"^refs/bus/seal/(?P<epoch>\d+)$",
}

def canon_payload(kind, epoch, wid, subject, parent, state_root, toolchain) -> bytes:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(
        {"kind": kind, "epoch": epoch, "wid": wid, "subject": subject,
         "parent": parent, "state_root": state_root, "toolchain": toolchain},
        sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).digest()
```

## 2. The LAW record

```python
GB1_UNIVOCAL = LawRecord(
    id="GB-1/univocal",

    trigger=(
        "on_push(refs/bus/**)",            # any push under the bus namespace
        "on_tick(journal)",                # periodic sweep: deadline / freeze checks
    ),

    condition=(
        "C1_single_ref:      push mutates exactly one ref; batch pushes rejected whole",
        "C2_grammar:         ref matches REF_GRAMMAR[kind]; kind inferred from path; "
                             "no other refs/bus/** path is writable by anyone",
        "C3_signer_valid:    wid ∈ roster(epoch_snapshot); ed25519 sig over "
                             "canon_payload(...) verifies against roster pubkey",
        "C4_anchored:        proposal.parent == bus.sealed_head AND "
                             "proposal.epoch == bus.epoch + 1 (strictly sequential)",
        "C5_deterministic:   verifier re-executes pinned toolchain on "
                             "(sealed_head.tree, epoch_input) → state_root MUST match "
                             "proposed root bit-for-bit",
        "C6_fresh_suffrage:  no existing object at refs/bus/votes/{e}/*/{wid}.sig "
                             "(one vote per worker per epoch, any candidate)",
        "C7_quorum_cert:     seal cites ≥ Q(N) distinct valid votes, all for ONE root "
                             "that exists as a proposal",
        "C8_pinned_toolchain: proposal.toolchain_digest == bus.refs/meta/toolchain",
    ),

    action={
        "ACCEPT":        "CAS update ref old→new (atomic compare-and-swap); append "
                         "journal entry {seq, law:GB-1, verdict, ref, sha}",
        "REJECT_QUORUM": "refuse push; journal note; no state mutation",
        "QUARANTINE":    "reject push + commit quarantine marker to refs/bus/meta/"
                         "quarantine (sole meta-write exemption); wid excluded from "
                         "vote/seal counts until reinstated by quorum",
        "FREEZE":        ">1 candidate certified (catastrophic, implies GR2 breach): "
                         "reject ALL non-meta pushes; human quorum required to unfreeze",
    },

    guardrail=(
        "GR1_immutability:  no force-update, no delete under refs/bus/**; "
                            "retraction is a forward tombstone commit on meta",
        "GR2_single_suffrage: one vote per (epoch, wid) regardless of outcome — "
                            "pre-receive scans existing votes before accepting",
        "GR3_safety_over_liveness: an uncertified epoch NEVER seals; if no candidate "
                            "reaches Q within EPOCH_DEADLINE_TICKS, bus HALTS — "
                            "minority may not proceed, ever",
        "GR4_self_bound_governance: roster and toolchain changes are themselves "
                            "commits requiring Q(N) signatures",
        "GR5_clockless:     all predicates and deadlines denominated in journal "
                            "ticks/epoch counters; zero wall-clock reads",
        "GR6_total_audit:   every verdict appended to refs/bus/journal; the journal "
                            "itself is quorum-sealed each epoch",
    ),

    tier=Tier.KERNEL,
)
register(GB1_UNIVOCAL)
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **id** | `GB-1/univocal` |
| **trigger** | `on_push(refs/bus/**)` · `on_tick(journal)` |
| **condition** | C1 single-ref · C2 ref-grammar · C3 signer∈roster+sig-valid · C4 parent=head, epoch=N+1 · C5 re-executed state_root matches · C6 one vote/(epoch,wid) · C7 seal cites ≥Q(N) votes for one root · C8 toolchain digest pinned |
| **action** | ACCEPT=CAS ref + journal · REJECT_QUORUM · QUARANTINE(divergent worker) · FREEZE(cert ambiguity) |
| **guardrail** | GR1 ref-immutability · GR2 single-suffrage · GR3 halt-not-fork · GR4 quorum-gated governance · GR5 clockless · GR6 total audit |
| **tier** | `KERNEL` (0) — non-bypassable |

## 3. Enforcement hook (the teeth)

```python
def evaluate(ev, bus):
    m = {k: re.match(p, ev.ref) for k, p in REF_GRAMMAR.items()}
    kind = next((k for k, v in m.items() if v), None)
    if ev.ref_count != 1 or kind is None:
        return Verdict(False, "GB-1/C1|C2", reason="malformed push")

    g = m[kind].groupdict(); e = int(g["epoch"]); wid = g["wid"]
    payload = canon_payload(kind, e, wid, g.get("root"), bus.sealed_head,
                            ev.state_root, ev.toolchain)
    if wid not in bus.roster(e) or not bus.verify(wid, payload, ev.sig):
        return Verdict(False, "GB-1/C3")

    if kind == "proposal":
        ok = (ev.parent == bus.sealed_head and e == bus.epoch + 1          # C4
              and ev.state_root == bus.reexecute(bus.sealed_head, e)       # C5 ← drift kill
              and ev.toolchain == bus.toolchain_digest)                    # C8
        return Verdict(ok, "GB-1/C4|C5|C8",
                       action=None if ok else ("QUARANTINE", wid))

    if kind == "vote":
        if bus.has_vote(e, wid):                                           # GR2/C6
            return Verdict(False, "GB-1/C6", reason="suffrage spent")
        return Verdict(g["root"] in bus.proposals(e), "GB-1/C6")

    if kind == "seal":
        certs = bus.certified_roots(e)                                     # C7
        if len(certs) > 1:
            return Verdict(False, "GB-1/C7", action=("FREEZE",))
        return Verdict(len(certs) == 1 and bus.vote_count(e, certs[0]) >= Q(bus.N),
                       "GB-1/C7")
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# .git/hooks/pre-receive  — Tier.KERNEL means this hook is not skippable
from mag.law import evaluate, PushEvent, open_bus
v = evaluate(PushEvent.from_stdin(), open_bus())
if not v.allow:
    print(f"LAW VIOLATION {v.clause}: {v.reason}", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)
sys.exit(0)
```

## Why this is actually one voice, no brain, no drift

- **Agreement:** Q = ⌈(2N+1)/3⌉ with N ≥ 3f+1. Two distinct roots cannot both collect Q votes, because any two Q-subsets of N workers intersect, and the common member would have voted twice — impossible under GR2. At most **one** truth per epoch. Not probabilistic. Structural.
- **Total order:** every seal is a CAS linearization on a single ref (`refs/bus/seal/e`). Concurrent seals for the *same* certified root are idempotent — first wins, second is a harmless reject.
- **No drift:** state is a pure function `Sₑ₊₁ = F(Sₑ, inputₑ)` with `F` pinned by toolchain digest. Every voter independently re-executes (cheap — stateless means nothing to sync). A drifting worker emits a wrong root, gets < Q votes, and is quarantined by C5. Divergence isn't punished after the fact; it's structurally infertile.
- **No brain:** no leader, no coordinator, no scheduler. Roles are symmetric; the only shared object is git itself, whose content-addressing gives free tamper-evidence.
- **Statelessness:** crash = replay the journal. Nothing lives in RAM across epochs.

## Worked micro-example (N=7, Q=5)

Epoch 41 sealed at `c₄₁`. Five workers propose root `r_a`; `w03`'s unpinned float op yields `r_x ≠ r_a`. Votes land: `r_a` ← w01,w02,w04,w05,w06,w07 (**6**); `r_x` ← w03's implicit self-vote only (**1**). `w05` seals → `c₄₂` = new head. C5 flags `w03`'s root against six independent re-executions → `QUARANTINE(w03)`. The bus spoke once, honestly, and the drift was buried childless. If only 4 workers were up: no candidate reaches 5 within 512 ticks → **HALT** (GR3) — silence beats schism.

The user wants me to design a LAW record for the Ghost-AOS "git-bus treaty" — a consensus mechanism for N stateless workers speaking as one honest voice without a central brain, no drift. They want it integrated into an existing `mag/law.py` enforcement registry as a LAW record with fields: id, trigger, condition, action, guardrail, tier.

Since I don't have the actual mag/law.py source (it's their internal system), I need to construct a plausible, exact schema based on the field list given: id, trigger, condition, action, guardrail, tier. I should define the law precisely enough to implement: the git-bus treaty is presumably that all workers coordinate through a git repository as the bus (commits/refs as messages), no direct peer-to-peer chatter, no central coordinator process. Stateless workers means each worker reads state from git and writes decisions back; consensus must be achieved via the git object model itself — refs are immutable-ish, commits are content-addressed, so the "one honest voice" emerges from deterministic rules over the DAG.

Key hard parts of consensus without central brain:
1. Single-writer per ref or deterministic merge function.
2. Quorum: N workers, each epoch produces exactly one canonical head. Without a leader, you need either (a) deterministic tie-break on commit hashes/content, or (b) a quorum certificate embedded in commits (e.g., 2f+1 signatures), or (c) hashgraph-style gossip about gossip.
3. No drift: stateless workers must derive identical state from identical inputs; determinism enforced by pinning interpreter/toolchain digests in the bus.
4. Fork resolution: two workers propose competing heads for same epoch → deterministic rule picks winner (e.g., lowest commit hash among valid quorum-certified candidates), losers rebase.

Design: The LAW record should encode:
- id: something like "LAW-GB-001" / "gitbus.univocal" 
- trigger: when a worker attempts to publish to the bus (push/commit to epoch branch) OR at epoch close.
- condition: the validity predicate — proposal must carry quorum certificate (≥ ⌈2N/3⌉+1 attestations from distinct worker identities signing (epoch, parent, state_root)), must be derived deterministically from parent + input batch, toolchain digest pinned, etc.
- action: accept → fast-forward canonical ref `refs/bus/head`; conflicting proposals → deterministic arbitration: select candidate with lexicographically smallest (cert_weight desc? no—must be deterministic and fork-safe) — simplest: smallest SHA over valid certified candidates; reject others; nonconforming pushes rejected by pre-receive hook; drift detection → worker quarantined.
- guardrail: no worker may push twice in same epoch; no human override; liveness floor (if quorum unavailable for T epochs, bus halts rather than forks — safety over liveness); rate limits; audit log append-only; guard against sybil (identity = key registered on bus).
- tier: enforcement tier, e.g., tier 0/kernel/hard-fail (non-bypassable).

Good: q = ⌈(2N+1)/3⌉.

Epoch mechanics: epoch e opens when previous epoch sealed. Workers pull `refs/bus/epoch/<e>/input`, compute deterministically, produce candidate commit with message carrying `epoch=e, parent=<sealed_head>, state_root=<hash>, toolchain_digest`, sign payload, push to `refs/bus/proposals/<e>/<worker_id>`. A proposal becomes "certified" when it collects q distinct signatures — collected how, without a brain? Workers observe proposals, verify determinism themselves (re-execute or check state root), then sign by pushing signature objects to `refs/bus/votes/<e>/<candidate_root>/<worker>.sig`. Certification check: count sigs. Then sealing: any worker observing a certified candidate may seal — but race between multiple seals → deterministic pick: if multiple candidates reach certification in same epoch (shouldn't if honest, but Byzantine possible since q intersection guarantees at most one certified value can be agreed... actually quorum intersection guarantees two different values cannot both get q votes if votes are single per worker per epoch). Enforce one-vote-per-worker-per-epoch via guardrail: pre-receive hook rejects second vote with same (epoch, worker) for different candidate. Then at most one candidate can gather q. Sealing rule: first valid certified seal attempt wins; seal commit itself must reference the certified set; guardrail: seal accepted only if cert verifiable at time of push.

Drift control: each worker's execution environment digest recorded; condition requires `state_root == expected deterministic function`; verification is re-execution by voters (they're stateless, they recompute anyway — cheap because stateless means pure function of bus state). So voting = re-execution + compare state_root. That's elegant: consensus by redundant deterministic recomputation; git stores everything; honesty = matching roots.

No-drift across epochs: parent linkage chain; any divergence breaks chain validation downstream.

Liveness halt: if no candidate certified within epoch timeout E_timeout (e.g., 10 min), bus enters HALT: canonical head unchanged, epoch increments only after recovery; guardrail forbids any fallback path that would let minority proceed.

from __future__ import annotations
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import IntEnum
import hashlib, json, re

class Tier(IntEnum):
    KERNEL = 0      # non-bypassable; violation freezes the bus
    HARD   = 1      # violation rejects the operation
    SOFT   = 2      # violation logs + warns

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LawRecord:
    id:         str
